new_statements.quote: Le Lumbu compte deux tons pertinents : le ton haut et le ton bas. [...] Les tons ont une fonction distinctive dans la langue. (p. 75) — La contrainte accentuelle dit que le ton flottant dérivé de la syllabe finale inaccentuée s'efface systématiquement (pp. 79-80) — 4.5.1 Elision vocalique sous syllabe inaccentuée. Dans le thème nominal ou radical verbal, la voyelle /a/ sous syllabe inaccentuée est systématiquement effacée, si la syllabe inaccentuée est en position post-radicale. Elle est éliminée en débit rapide de la voix, si la syllabe inaccentuée est en position finale. (p. 99)
new_statements.translation: Lumbu has two distinctive tones: high and low. [...] Tones have a distinctive function in the language. (p. 75) — The accentual constraint says that the floating tone derived from the unaccented final syllable is systematically deleted (pp. 79-80) — 4.5.1 Vowel elision under an unaccented syllable. In the nominal stem or verbal radical, the vowel /a/ under an unaccented syllable is systematically deleted if the unaccented syllable is in post-radical position. It is eliminated in rapid speech if the unaccented syllable is in final position. (p. 99)
new_statements.citation: Gamille, Léa Ghislaine. 2013. Elements de description phonologique et morphologique du Lumbu, langue bantu (B44) du Gabon parlée à Mayumba. PhD thesis, Université Sorbonne Nouvelle – Paris 3.
new_statements.locator: Phonologie §2.1 p. 75; §2.5 'Contrainte accentuelle' pp. 79-80; §4.5.1 p. 99 (PDF pp. 76, 81, 100)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Lumbu is a two-tone language (H/L, with HL/LH contours, floating tones, downdrift). The thesis never states where accent falls; it only labels post-radical and word-final stem syllables as 'inaccentuées' (their /a/ reduces to schwa or deletes; their derived floating L tone is erased). By implication the accented syllable is the radical (stem-initial) syllable, i.e. the first syllable after the class prefix — a common Bantu pattern — but this is an inference, not a stated rule.
new_statements.exceptions: Reduction/elision of the unaccented /a/ is rate-dependent: post-radical /a/ always deleted, final /a/ only in rapid speech, otherwise schwa (pp. 48, 99-100).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (nominal stem / verbal radical); the term 'syllabe inaccentuée' appears only in the vowel-elision and floating-tone rules, never in a prosodic section. Variety: Lumbu of Mayumba (Gabon).
new_statements.identity_note: All primary sources describe the Gabonese variety of Mayumba (Gamille 2013; Blanchon 1984 conte from a Mayumba speaker); Blanchon 1990 uses Gamba (northern) Lumbu data and notes tonal differences between the two; the Congo (Banda) variety is covered only by the inaccessible Mfouhou works. Language names: Lumbu, Yilumbu, Luumbu, Loumbou, yi-lumbu (Guthrie B44); all under glottocode lumb1249.

sources.quote: Le Lumbu compte deux tons pertinents : le ton haut et le ton bas. [...] Les tons ont une fonction distinctive dans la langue. (p. 75) — La contrainte accentuelle dit que le ton flottant dérivé de la syllabe finale inaccentuée s'efface systématiquement (pp. 79-80) — 4.5.1 Elision vocalique sous syllabe inaccentuée. sources.locator: Phonologie §2.1 p. 75; §2.5 'Contrainte accentuelle' pp. 79-80; §4.5.1 p. 99 (PDF pp. 76, 81, 100)
sources.note: Tonal language: two level tones H and B, contours HB/BH, fixed vs floating tones, downdrift and final lowering (§2 Tons, pp. 75-82). No explicit statement of where accent/stress falls; the thesis nevertheless uses an undefined notion of 'syllabe inaccentuée' for post-radical and word-final syllables, whose /a/ is reduced to schwa or elided (p. 48, §4.5.1 p. 99, p. 225) and whose derived floating low tone is deleted ('contrainte accentuelle', pp. 79-80). No accented syllable is ever named; the implication is that the stem-initial (radical) syllable is the accented one.

sources.note: §4.6.3 (p. 114): 'Yilumbu is a tone language with two distinctive tone levels, high (H) and low (L)'; HL and LH melodies; three tonal classes following Blanchon; tonal perturbations by context. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1990. The great *HL split in Bantu group B40. Pholia 5: 17-51.
sources.note: Tone classes of B40 nominals; B44 data from the Gamba variety, note 5: in Mayumba Lumbu tone-classes B (°HL) and D (°HH) are no longer distinct (p. 24). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1988. Première approche d'une tonologie comparée du groupe bantou B40. Pholia 3: 37-62 (approx.).
sources.note: Comparative tonology: Punu (B43) and Lumbu (B44) 'n'ont aucun relèvement tonal', giving a jerky melody with isolated H peaks between L stretches. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1987. Les classes 9, 10 et 11 dans le groupe bantou B40 (section 2: B44 yi-lumbu de Mayumba). Pholia 2: 5-22 (approx.).
sources.note: Noun-class morphology and tone of prefixes; nothing on stress. Pholia vols 4, 6-9 were also downloaded and scanned for 'lumbu': only ethnohistorical and bibliographic mentions.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1984. Présentation du yi-lumbu dans ses rapports avec le yi-punu et le ci-vili à travers un conte traditionnel. Pholia 1: 7-35.
sources.note: Text with notes on segmental and tonal differences from Punu and Vili: Yi-Lumbu 'possède un ton descendant à partir d'un registre plus haut que le registre haut' (p. 8); Mayumba Lumbu 'semble avoir perdu l'opposition °HH/°HB' (p. 22). Nothing on stress/accent.
